title: A healing and a mercy
hook: We send down in the Qur'an what is a healing and a mercy (17:82)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the unseen, and your line, faith in the unseen. Today, what the book says it does for the one who hears it.

A desert camp, somewhere in Arabia. A small band of the Prophet's companions has stopped near a tribe that won't host them. That night the tribe's chief is stung by a scorpion, and nothing they try helps. Someone comes over: does any of you know a cure? One companion says he does. He sits by the chief and recites the Fatiha over him, again and again, blowing lightly as he goes. The hadith, in al-Bukhari, says the chief got up as if he'd been freed from a rope.

Back in Medina, they told the Prophet ﷺ, and he asked the reciter: how did you know it was a ruqyah, a recitation for healing? He approved what they'd done. That story sits behind a word the Qur'an uses about itself. Surah seventeen, verse eighty-two, in Pickthall's translation: "And We reveal of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for believers." The word for healing is shifa'. Elsewhere the Qur'an calls itself a healing for what is in the breasts, the hearts, in surah ten, and a guidance and a healing in surah forty-one. Notice which sickness these verses point to first. Commentators say it's in the heart: doubt, fear, grief, a restless mind. The book is a mercy for that. Scholars also cite hadith like the scorpion story to hold that its recitation can be a means of healing for the body. And Islamic teaching doesn't set this against medicine. A hadith in al-Bukhari says Allah has not sent down a disease without sending down a cure for it. So shifa' comes in two hands at once: a doctor's prescription in one, a verse in the other. Neither has to cancel the other out. On a low day, the second hand is the one people sometimes forget they have.
screen: `MEDICINE IN ONE HAND, A VERSE IN THE OTHER.`

segments.voice: You don't have to be low right now; this is practice for the day you are. Bring to mind a short verse or line you know, the Fatiha or anything from this year that stayed with you, or simply the words a healing and a mercy. Say it slowly three times, letting each word take a full breath, and notice whether anything in your chest loosens, even a little.
Shifa'. Healing. The Qur'an calls itself a healing and a mercy for believers, first for the heart, and recited, by the hadith, for the body too. Today's word.
Your line: a healing. One line, held close, for the low days ahead. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: In ruqyah, Muslims recite the Fatiha, the last two surahs and other verses over someone who is ill, alongside medical treatment; a hadith in al-Bukhari says Allah sent down no disease without its cure.

chat.says: If the Qur'an is a healing, does that mean I can skip the doctor?
options: No: a hadith says every disease has a cure, so medicine and verse go together.
Yes: a verse can only work once you stop all your medicine.
No: the Qur'an only heals the body, so it can't help with grief.
chat.meaning: Shifa' comes in two hands: the Qur'an, a healing first for the heart, and medicine, since Allah sent down a cure for every disease.
